title: Why Sewer Gas Escapes into Your Building
description: Sewer gas escaping into a building is often caused by a compromised water seal in the drainage trap. When plumbing fixtures go unused for extended periods, the water inside the P-trap evaporates, opening a direct pathway for sewer gases to enter. Additionally, poor vent pipe design or atmospheric pressure fluctuations can siphon water out of the trap during drainage. Regular usage, replenishing traps, and ensuring proper DWV system venting are essential to maintaining the safe, continuous liquid barrier that protects indoor air quality and occupants safety.

Why Sewer Gas Escapes into Your Building

Sewer gas escaping into a building is often caused by a compromised water seal in the drainage trap. When plumbing fixtures go unused for extended periods, the water inside the P-trap evaporates, opening a direct pathway for sewer gases to enter. Additionally, poor vent pipe design or atmospheric pressure fluctuations can siphon water out of the trap during drainage. Regular usage, replenishing traps, and ensuring proper DWV system venting are essential to maintaining the safe, continuous liquid barrier that protects indoor air quality and occupants safety.
